sections.content_markdown: As some modern English grammar books have pointed out, it is important to be aware that, strictly speaking, English does not have a future tense. Rather the language has a number of verb forms that can be used to express future time, predictions, intentions, promises, etc.

Read the following conversations and notice the use of *will*, *shall* and *won't* to refer to the future time:

a. : How old are you, sir?
: I'll be 56 on the second of next month. I'll retire next year.
: Well, what will you do after retirement? Have you thought of something?
: No, not really. Maybe I will travel for a while. I've always wanted to do that.

b. : Oh dear! I've forgotten to bring my medicine.
: Don't worry. I'll go and buy it for you. There's a pharmacy down the street.
